content.text:
Progress! All 3 GC stems (with GAAA loop) fold correctly. Only the 3 AU stems (23-30, 47-54, 71-78) are missing — they're too weak. I'll convert them to GU wobble pairs (G•U), which are stronger than A-U and still won't be complementary to the GC stems. Stem = GUGAAACA (G-U, U-G wobble pair): 23=G,24=U,29=U,30=G... wait that's G-U and U-G — let me make it G-U/G-U which is symmetric and won't be GC-complementary.

Actually, the issue: AUGAAAUA folds as `....((....))`? No — the AU stems just don't form. Let me try GU wobbles: stem positions 23,24 pair with 30,29. Pair 23-30 = G-U, 24-29 = U-G. Sequence: 23=G,24=U,29=U,30=G → GUAA...AUG. Hmm that's GUAAA AUG. Let me use GUGAAACA: 23=G,24=U,25-28=GAAA,29=A,30=C → pairs G-C (23-30) and U-A (24-29). Strong GC! But that's same as stem GC pattern which caused cross-talk earlier.

The key insight: alternating GC and GC-complementary patterns caused pseudoknots. But now I have a strong outer GC + 3 inner GC stems with GAAA loops and A-spacers working. The AU stems are the problem. Let me just make ALL stems GC with GAAA loops but add GU wobble at the closing pair to break symmetry, OR add more A spacers between to fully isolate. Actually the current 3 GC stems WORK with AAAA spacers. Let me convert AU stems to GC too — the pseudoknot issue earlier was specific to the all-GC version, let me retest with full GC.

The earlier all-GC version had pseudoknots because stem2 paired with stem3 (long-range). With GAAA tetraloops (which I now have), the local hairpin is much more stable, so pseudoknots may not form. Let me try all-GC stems with GAAA loops.
